metadata.name: Supply Chain Attack → Persistent Access → Widespread Compromise

stage_1_identify_target.description: Attacker identifies popular open-source or commercial software with significant user base

implementation.method: Analyze GitHub star count, npm downloads, production usage

detection_points: Unusual project interest/forking
Attacker reconnaissance (GitHub API queries, dependency analysis)

stage_2_compromise_maintainer.description: Attacker gains access to project maintainer's GitHub/GitLab account

implementation.method: Phishing maintainer, credential stuffing, or social engineering
attack_vectors: Phishing email with malicious GitHub action file
Dependency confusion (publish higher version on public registry)

detection_points: Unusual authentication method (new device, new location)
Unlikely commit times (middle of night, weekend)
Commit emails differ from maintainer's registered email

stage_3_inject_malicious_code.description: Attacker injects backdoor into legitimate codebase

implementation.method: Add small malicious code to legitimate commit, disguise as bug fix
evasion_techniques: Single-line code change: import legitimate_module; malicious_code_hidden_in_module_internals
Comment obfuscation: # Optimization for legacy systems (actually launches C2)
GitHub Actions workflow modification: new job that exfiltrates build secrets
Conditional compilation: payload only activates for specific environment variables
payload_characteristics: Minimal code footprint (1-5 lines in main code)
Hidden in initialization routine (hard to review)
Phone-home payload: reaches out to attacker C2 server

detection_points: Code review catches suspicious imports
Unusual network calls in package initialization
Build log anomalies (unexpected outbound connections)
Dependency analysis tools flag unusual behavior

stage_4_release_malicious_version.description: Attacker publishes poisoned version to package registry

implementation.method: Push new version to npm/PyPI/Maven Central
distribution_strategy: Version supersedes current stable: users auto-update via package manager
Release notes appear normal: 'Bug fixes and performance improvements'

detection_points: SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) analysis detects new dependency version
Build pipeline behavioral changes (new network connections)
Security vendor feeds flag malicious hash
CDN log analysis shows unusual traffic patterns

stage_5_activate_payload.description: When package is installed/imported by organizations, payload activates

activation_conditions: Automatic: Every time package imported (npm require, Python import)
Conditional: Only activates if specific environment detected (production)
Delayed: Waits 24-48 hours before activating (avoid immediate detection)
payload_functions: Steal build secrets (AWS keys, GitHub tokens from environment)
Register reverse shell callback to C2 server
Persist via cron job or systemd service

detection_points: Build pipeline outbound network connections
EDR detects background process spawning
Package sandbox detection (attempted file/network access)
Application performance monitoring (API slowdown from exfiltration)

stage_6_exfiltrate_secrets.description: Attacker exfiltrates build secrets, API keys, database credentials

implementation.method: Scan environment variables and configuration files for secrets
targets: API_KEYS for payment processors, cloud services
exfiltration_method: Cloud storage (S3 bucket, cloud-hosted attacker infrastructure)

detection_points: Build log analysis: unexpected curl/wget commands
Network egress monitoring: unusual domains/IPs
DLP (Data Loss Prevention): credential patterns in outbound traffic
Build artifact analysis: inspect package before deployment

stage_7_lateral_movement.technique: Lateral Movement via Compromised Build Secrets
stage_7_lateral_movement.description: Using stolen credentials, attacker accesses downstream systems

implementation.method: Use exfiltrated GitHub token to access source code, AWS key to spin up resources
actions: Clone private repositories (gain source code access)
Deploy malicious infrastructure (EC2 instance, Lambda function)
Modify CI/CD pipeline (inject malicious step into every build)
Access artifact repositories (poison container images, libraries)

detection_points: GitHub: Unusual repository clones from new IP
AWS CloudTrail: API calls from new geographic location
CI/CD pipeline: modification to build steps
Container registry: new images pushed by automated account

stage_8_persistent_access.description: Attacker establishes persistent access for long-term exploitation

implementation.method: Create admin user, install SSH key, modify CI/CD configuration
persistence_mechanisms: Add SSH key to GitHub organization (backdoor account creation)
Create IAM user in AWS with programmatic access

detection_points: GitHub audit log: new SSH keys added
AWS IAM: new users created
Access pattern changes (account activity outside normal hours)
Privilege escalation attempts

stage_9_widespread_compromise.description: Compromised package dependencies reach thousands of organizations

implementation.method: Malicious package automatically pulled by dependent projects
attacker_leverage: Ability to compromise all build systems
Data theft from millions of users

detection_points: Security vendor alerts on malicious hash
Coordinated CISO notifications
Organizational SBOM analysis
Threat intelligence sharing (CISA alerts)

critical_detection_gaps.gap: Malicious code injected looks legitimate (single-line change)
critical_detection_gaps.impact: Code review misses backdoor; automatically merged
critical_detection_gaps.fix: Behavioral analysis of imports; sandboxed package testing

critical_detection_gaps.gap: Package registry has no verification process
critical_detection_gaps.impact: Malicious package published to registry without review
critical_detection_gaps.fix: Mandatory code review for package updates; signature verification

critical_detection_gaps.impact: Malicious version automatically installed in 1-7 days
critical_detection_gaps.fix: Stage updates (test in dev, then staging, then prod); hold updates for review

critical_detection_gaps.gap: Build secrets stored in environment variables
critical_detection_gaps.impact: Exfiltrated secrets give attacker full access to downstream systems
critical_detection_gaps.fix: Rotate build secrets frequently; use temporary STS tokens instead

critical_detection_gaps.gap: No anomaly detection on build pipeline behavior
critical_detection_gaps.fix: Baseline normal build behavior; alert on deviations (new imports, network calls)

incident_response_drill_objectives: Code review catches malicious injection before merge
Dependency verification alerts on new version
Threat intelligence feed flags malicious hash
Downstream systems quarantined before lateral movement
Build secrets rotated before attacker uses them
Post-compromise forensics identify all affected systems
